GROUP BY item_no, qtr
ORDER BY item_no, qtr
"}

## Findings (calendar quarters, item-level basis: gross sales less cost of goods at the unit cost valid on the sale date)

**Insulated bottle (A-100)** and **Field jacket (B-200)**, both supplied by Meridian Supply, sold the same volume and at the same list price in both quarters (400 units / $12,000 sales for the bottle, 200 units / $10,000 sales for the jacket, in each quarter — `pos_sales`). Nothing changed on the revenue side. What changed was unit cost, per Meridian's invoiced cost (`ledger`, supplier_invoice rows):

| Item | Q1 2026 unit cost | Q2 2026 unit cost | Q1 GP | Q2 GP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-100 Insulated bottle | $15.00 | $18.00 (+20%) | $6,000 | $4,800 |
| B-200 Field jacket | $30.00 | $33.00 (+10%) | $4,000 | $3,400 |
| **Combined** | | | **$10,000** | **$8,200** |

Combined gross sales were $22,000 in both quarters, so combined gross margin fell from **45.45%** (Q1) to **37.27%** (Q2), a drop of $1,800 in gross profit on flat revenue.

## Why it fell
Meridian's terms set a 500-unit-per-quarter volume break across all Meridian products; whichever tier a quarter's orders earn sets the unit cost for the *next* quarter. The Q1 2026 Meridian purchase order (`ledger` J00015) was deliberately cut from 620 to 470 units "per cash plan" — 30 units short of the 500-unit break. That miss (confirmed by `quarter_units_ordered` = 470 for Q1 2026) pushed both items into the higher "below-break" cost tier for Q2 2026 ($18 and $33 instead of $15 and $30), which is exactly what ate the margin. Prices were unchanged throughout, so this is a pure cost-side effect, not a pricing one.

## What would restore it — and a heads-up
Placing at least 500 combined Meridian units in a quarter earns the lower tier for the following quarter, restoring A-100 to $15 and B-200 to $30 and recovering the $1,800/quarter. However, the Q2 2026 Meridian order (`ledger` J00018) was also only 480 units — again short of 500 — so Q3 2026 unit costs are already locked at the higher tier too. To recover the margin starting Q4 2026, Harbor needs to place Meridian orders totaling **500 units or more across all Meridian products in the current quarter (Q3 2026)**. I did not place any order or change any price; this is a purchasing-timing decision, not a pricing one, so no approval action was needed from me today.

ANSWER: The insulated bottle and field jacket earned $10,000 combined gross profit in Q1 2026 (45.45% margin) versus $8,200 in Q2 2026 (37.27% margin) on flat unit volume and flat prices in both quarters; the drop was caused entirely by Meridian Supply's unit cost rising from $15 to $18 (bottle) and $30 to $33 (jacket) because Harbor's Q1 2026 Meridian order (470 units) missed the 500-unit quarterly volume break by 30 units. Since Q2 2026's Meridian order (480 units) also missed the break, Q3 2026 costs are already locked at the higher tier; restoring margin requires ordering 500+ combined Meridian units in the current quarter (Q3 2026) to earn the lower tier for Q4.
